entries.title: Genesis 4:1
segments:
Cain; meaning possession. 
 
  A man; man-child, a son. 
 
  From the Lord; that is, by intercession with him, and with his aid. Some suppose she thought this son to be the promised Seed, who should bruise the serpent's head.

entries.title: Genesis 4:2
segments: Abel; signifying vanity.

entries.title: Genesis 4:3
segments: In process of time; probably at the end of some stated time appointed to worship God.

entries.title: Genesis 4:4
segments: Had respect; received it with favor, and showed that he accepted it; because it pointed forward to the atoning blood of Christ, and showed faith in what God had revealed concerning him.
In the declaration that the seed of the woman should bruise the serpent's head, and in the appointment of sacrifices,
, God revealed the certainty of a coming Saviour, and laid a foundation for faith, by the exercise of which men might be justified, and for Christ's sake be accepted as righteous.

entries.title: Genesis 4:5
segments:
Had not respect; he did not accept it.  It was not an expression of faith in a coming Saviour, and was not offered with a right spirit. 
 
  His countenance fell; he looked sad, angry, and sullen. 
 
Faith in what God has revealed with regard to the Redeemer, and the way of life through him, is, to those who know this revelation, essential to acceptable worship.  He that rejects the Son rejects also the Father, and will be rejected by him.

entries.title: Genesis 4:7
segments:
Sin lieth at the door; according to some, crouched at thy door, like a beast of prey, ready to destroy thee; according to others, a sin-offering (such as I require) lieth at the door, by offering which in a right spirit, thou mayest gain my favor. 
 
  Thou shalt rule over him; Cain, being the eldest son according to his birthright would have preeminence over Abel.

entries.title: Genesis 4:9
segments:
My brother's keeper; one whose business it is to watch over and take care of him. 
 
Sins have a close connection, and the commission of one leads to the commission of others.  He who will commit murder will also tell lies.

entries.title: Genesis 4:10
segments: Blood crieth; calleth for the punishment of him who shed it.

entries.title: Genesis 4:11
segments: From the earth; or ground, which would not yield him its increase as before, and would thus testify against his sin.

entries.title: Genesis 4:12
segments: A fugitive--a vagabond; driven from God's presence and the home of Adam.

entries.title: Genesis 4:14
segments:
Face of the earth; the land where he had dwelt. 
 
  From thy face; from the place where God manifested his special presence, he would be expelled. 
 
  Shall slay me; he knew they would think that he deserved to die for killing his brother, and was afraid they would treat him accordingly. 
 
A murderer feels that he deserves to die; and when he is put to death, often acknowledges that it is just.

entries.title: Genesis 4:15
segments:
Seven-fold; he shall be more severly punished. 
 
  Set a mark upon Cain; more literally, appointed to Cain a sign, that is, some miraculous token.  He was to live a vagabond, as a monument of the guilt of murder and of the wrath of God against it.

entries.title: Genesis 4:16
segments: Land of Nod; that is, of vagrancy.

entries.title: Genesis 4:17
segments: His wife; it is supposed that Cain was married before he murdered Abel.

entries.title: Genesis 4:19
segments: Two wives; this is the first instance mentioned of a violation of the law of marriage, by taking more than one wife.  It shows that men had become very corrupt, and this course tended to make them worse.

entries.title: Genesis 4:20
segments: The father; the inventor of a business, or he who makes great improvements in it, is, in Hebrew, called the father of those who pursue it.

entries.title: Genesis 4:22
segments: Instructor--and iron; or, forger of every instrument of brass and iron.

entries.title: Genesis 4:24
segments: Lamech seventy and seven; God had said,

, that should any one kill Cain, his death sould be avenged seven-fold; and Lamech says his would be avenged seventy and seven; implying that in his own estimation he was much less guilty than Cain; and that he who should kill him, would be punished much more severely than he who should kill Cain.

entries.title: Genesis 4:25
segments: Seth; meaning appointed or substituted in place of Abel.

entries.title: Genesis 4:26
segments: To call upon the name of the Lord; they separated themselves from the wicked, maintained the public worship of God, and were thus recognized as his visible people.  It is generally thought that they were "the sons of God," mentioned in

. 
 
If men would possess the character and receive the reward of God's people, they must separate themselves from his enemies, publicly maintain his worship, and show themselves to be his friends.
